title: OFT independent task transforms versus shared Mirror orthogonal views
hypothesis: On a shared frozen linear feature map, a low-dimensional one-plane orthogonal Mirror coordinate can reconstruct aligned task-specific orthogonal maps with substantially less serialized task state than independent OFT matrices; generic independent rotations may require factorized or private state.
physical_object: one frozen shared two-layer feature network
mirror_coordinate: one angle per task on a fixed two-channel plane
controls: independent native OFT dense orthogonal transform per task

development.allowed: validate parameterization, matrix orientation, task generation, fitting, serialization and metrics; select only before fresh

success_gate: Aligned family: Mirror output NRMSE <=1e-4 and total payload <=50% of independent OFT payload in every fresh world. Generic orthogonal stratum maps private-state boundary.
failure_gate: Mirror aligned NRMSE >0.01 or payload >80% of OFT at matched quality. No Mirror-specific claim if fixed-plane native coefficient control matches it.
boundaries: No text-to-image or natural task quality claim
OFT is prior art; orthogonality itself is not a novelty claim
Task identity is provided; no router tested
